## VERDICT

# `revise-before-implementation`

**Not because the architecture is wrong.**\
The core thesis is sound and evidence-driven: one sovereign write function, a pure planner, server-owned cascade and inverse, and a milestone order that is a genuine gated ascension.\
D5's kill of `server/commit.mjs` survives a hostile Earned-Exposure attack (two consumers, `store.js:240`/`:260`, each cancelling a different axis, `:242` vacuous validate and `:261` vacuous load `[V]`); D16's sovereignty layering matches the real import graph exactly `[V]`; D1's ruling to keep the <=32 KiB log out of `Model.toJSON()` is A12 reasoning reached independently and correctly (`rest.js:117`, `:223` `[V]`); section 4's invariants-become-tests wiring is the cleanest instance of A14 signal 6 in the arc.\
The verdict is `revise` because **seven items are cheap now and expensive-to-impossible later**, and because the plan's own evidentiary discipline has a proven hole: the `[V]/[I]/[A]` marking held on ~50 spot-checked claims and **failed on all four unmarked ones** - `docs/history/` (absent `[V]`), "standing principle 1" x2 (absent from the entire tree `[V]`), and the Slides-binding premise (section Deltas D4), which is false in a way that silently deletes a shipped capability.\
Two of the seven - the M4 irreversibility gate over 17 untracked user files and the reversal of three locked `SCOPE.md` decisions - are **authority items that cannot be ratified retroactively**; one - the I2 source-scan test - guards a property that holds *today* `[V, exhaustive grep: server-side `model.put/set/del` appears only at `store.js:104-106`]` and becomes forensic archaeology once it breaks, because every stored inverse below the breach is silently corrupt with no error at the time of corruption.\
Fix the seven, and this becomes `pass-with-guardrails` without touching a single design ruling.

### Mechanics explicitly marked **not materially implicated** (anti-decoration record)
- **A5 - Pre-Attentive Rendering** - the ~300 ms budget is not at risk in a 65-entity / 6912 B document `[V, measured]`.
- **A11 - Token Accounting, Economic Telemetry** - structurally inapplicable: drawv2 invokes no model, so it cannot meter tokens. The audited proxy is round-trips and bytes per agent intent, stated as a proxy.
- **A6 - Zero Transcription** (literal artifact-to-artifact sense) - drawv2 has no proposal/decision-record chain; it surfaces only obliquely via the 409 re-derivation.
- **A11 - D4's "60 transactions -> 1"** - deliberately **not** claimed as an A11 win: it is a browser metric, and `app/src/*` is outside the A11/A12 fence.

### Integrity note - struck and corrected citations
**Four citations were struck at the W22 gate and do not appear above; one sub-claim was struck; six were downgraded.**\
Struck: **A3-T8** (`Hub.broadcast`'s 4th positional parameter) as *decorative* - Semantic Bit-Masking governs message shape, not parameter style; delete A3 and nobody writes `except` differently.\
**A0-T1** as a distinct finding - triple-counted with A4-F6 and A11-T2, which land the identical defect with stronger mandates; the delta survives under A11.\
**A2-D1** and **A14-D13** as subsumed by better-specified siblings.\
Sub-claim struck: A3-T4's `toJSON() === {}` case, unreachable (`model.mjs:250-257` always emits meta + 5 collections + selection `[V]`).\
Downgraded: A5-1's severity (an *underspecification*, not a contradiction - see Tension T1), A3-T3 to supporting with a set correction, A9-R5 to supporting (rests on `[A]` external Cloud Run behaviour), A11-delta-4 to optional (already true today), A5-D6 to conditional, A9-R1's `google-token.json` glob sub-point to minor (`docker-compose.yml:12-13` separates the volumes `[V]`).

### Out of force - recorded so it cannot be cited
**A2 Isomorphic Specification** (`declarative`) is **NOT in force** and was excluded before mapping began. drawv2 has no reconciler and no manifest: the wire vocabulary is imperative (`put`/`set`/`del`, `validate.js:118-122`), `applyOps` is an ordered instruction loop (`store.js:102-108`), `FIELDS` is a table of compiled-in predicate closures rather than a parsed spec (`validate.js:60-85`), `app/src/schema.js:63` carries a *second* compiled-in meta shape, nothing in the tree parses `SCOPE.md` (exhaustive grep returns source comments only), and the one reconciler-shaped candidate - Slides push - is an explicit-button, one-way, wipe-and-recreate projection `[V, all]`.\
**The plan moves further away** by deleting `push {doc}`, its only whole-state assertion verb.\
Two overturn attempts were made at the W22 stage and both failed.\
**A2 must not be cited to justify the op log, the Change record, or `expect`** - `expect` is compare-and-swap, not reconciliation.\
Audited and confirmed: no slice attempted it.

## LAYERED APPLICATION

| Layer | Primary axioms | How the design behaves | Holds? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Umbrella / intent** | A0 | The Director expresses *what* ("delete the selection", "put a group here") and the substrate owns *how* - cascade, inverse, ids, ordering, narrowing. D12/D10/D9(b) move four deterministic computations off every caller. This is the plan's genuine organising principle. | **HOLDS.** The only intent-layer defect is attention, not architecture - routed to the Director layer. |
| **Substrate / state** | A1, A5, A7 | Source of truth becomes the server: `meta.version` minted in `commit`, one write path, doc+log published in one atomic `rename`. But **the Log is authoritative for undo from M2 and durable only at M5**, unqueryable until M6, and `Log.version` has no persisted source at all. On restart, `Store.init` skips a rejecting file (`store.js:124-128`) and reseeds when the store empties (`store.js:142`) - an authorized entity then receives a **plausible, complete, wrong answer with HTTP 200**. | **DOES NOT HOLD as sequenced.** Fix: D5, D8, D9, D12, D19. |
| **Specification / configuration** | ~~A2~~, A11 | A2 is out of force, so the only spec-drift question that binds is A11's: is a deterministic rule mechanized or left for an actor to remember? Mostly mechanized - I2 is *stated* as a source scan, D4 inverts rather than wraps. But `expect` is optional on the destructive verb, and `docs/spec/SCOPE.md` asserts the opposite of the running wire from M2 to M6 - in the file an LLM controller reads to learn the protocol. | **HOLDS WITH GUARDRAILS.** Fix: D6, D14, D3. |
| **Composition / boundaries** | A3 | Each substrate owns one concern and the import graph proves it. Surfaces are earned, not anticipated - D5 kills a module parameterised on a port nobody varies. Two boundary defects remain: one file format co-owned by four modules through byte-splicing, and the entity-shape fact split across a boundary that cannot legally be crossed. | **HOLDS WITH GUARDRAILS.** Fix: D6, D17, D18. |
| **Knowledge / audit** | A4 | Rationale is migrated on deletion three times; section 8.1 banks disproofs; section 3 names a *Trading away* line on 11 of 16 rulings (absent on **D8, D12, D16** `[V]`). Against that: **three phantom citations authorise three deletions**, the plan itself has no durable address, and eviction - a designed, bounded loss - is reported at no surface (`truncated` appears once in the plan, `evicted` never `[V]`). | **DOES NOT HOLD.** Fix: D2, D7, D13, D22, D24. |
| **Perception / context** | A5, A12 | The browser gains a live change stream and undo state as perceived fields. The **agent gains nothing**: it cannot read lock ownership, cannot subscribe to changes, and cannot read the log until M6 - while from M2 its committed writes become reversible by another actor. And `GET .../history`, the one endpoint built for it, has no specified projection over records carrying both `ops` and `inverse`. | **DOES NOT HOLD.** Fix: D8, D10, D12, D21. |
| **Collaboration / operations** | A6, A7 | Administrative handoff genuinely removed on the *forward* path - the dependency graph is inferred once, server-side. On the *reverse* path it is added: the human's remedy for agent damage is "reclaim, then press Ctrl+Z N times", N unknown and unbounded, over a lock that any polling loop can re-acquire. Failures: a rejected write is a bare string `console.warn`ed (`sync.js:139` `[V]`); an acked-then-lost commit is silent; the load-bearing fanout has no error boundary. | **HOLDS WITH GUARDRAILS** on the forward path; **does not hold** on the reverse. ## TENSIONS

| # | Tension | Axioms genuinely opposed | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | **The ack must carry the server's expansion (so the origin converges) vs the ack must stay minimal.** D7 excludes the origin from fanout; D12 says the browser "applies the server's expanded change when it echoes back"; section 1.5/section 1.7 sketch `ack{version,canUndo,canRedo}` with no `ops`. section 2.3 deletes the browser's cascade. | A5 (parity) x A12 (bounded payload) - *apparent only* | **Underspecification, not contradiction** - D7's own sentence, *"the origin gets the same information on its `ack`"*, resolves it toward D12. The A5 slice's derived consequence chain (orphaned links, wrong hulls, "permanent divergence") holds only under the reading D7 rejects and was **downgraded**. No real A12 cost: the ack is bounded by the 2000-op request cap and is *narrower* than today's full-snapshot broadcast. **Resolution: pin the field list in the plan text before M1 fixes `commit`'s return type (D10), and restate I7 (D9), which is a false-green under either reading.** |

Rules implementation must not violate.\
**Every one is mechanized** - a test, a scanner, a runtime assertion, or a boot condition.\
None is left for an actor to remember.

|---|---|---|---|
| **G-1** | Promotion to trunk is gated by a deterministic proof, not a habit. | `npm run gate` = 183-suite + I2 scan + unmarked-claim scan + `docs/spec/COMMIT.md` exists; installed `pre-push` hook. | **Before M1** |
| **G-2** | No module other than `model/ops.mjs#applyOps` calls `model.put/set/del` **or `model.load`** on the server. | Source scan with a single allow-listed site; the allow-list file is the durable record of any future exception. Runtime assertion in `install()` that the `Log` is replaced in the same call. | **M1**, standing |

| **G-5** | Every invariant I1-I14 names the milestone gate that proves it; **zero unassigned**. | Traceability table in `docs/spec/COMMIT.md`, re-checked at each milestone close. I2->G-2, I11->M3, I12->G-8. | **M1**, each milestone |
| **G-6** | New authority code is certified where it ships, not one layer up. | `undo`/`redo`/`Log` battery (I5 round trip; cursor/eviction property test) runs at **M1**; M5 re-runs I5 across `new Store()` as the *persistence* proof only. | **M1** |

| **G-8** | `version` and `seq` are monotonic **per diagram across restarts**; a stored inverse is never applied against a state it did not produce. | `Log.serialize()` emits `version`; `Log.from(json, meta.version)` seeds. Plus a runtime post-condition inside `flush()` asserting `meta.version === log.version` - fires on all 183 existing tests and every new one. | **M5** (assertion **M1**) |

**Audit falsifiers, recorded so this artifact can be disproved.**\
This audit was decorative if: (a) a cold actor six months on can reconstruct *why* undo is global, *why* the log lives in the diagram file, *why* `version` is a counter, and *why* `push` was deleted - without this session; (b) M4 ships, 17 files survive, and the Director's reaction is "I'd already assumed that"; (c) three mutants of `plan()` - a dropped cascade op, a key-projected inverse on an *added* key, and a second server module calling `model.set` - are all killed by the ~20 tests M1 already names without D6 and D25.\
The claim is that **(c) survives on the third mutant**, and that is precisely why I2 must be mechanized rather than believed.

# THE DECISIONS FOR THE DIRECTOR

Four decisions.\
Everything else in this audit is substrate work that does not need you.

1. **M4 rewrites your 17 real diagram files irreversibly, and the plan never asks.** Approve it as a named gate before M1 starts, with a dry-run-and-verify migration script and the backup retained until M6 - *recommendation: approve on those terms; the plan's current gate asserts only a file count and then `rm -rf`s the only copy of untracked data.*

2. **The plan reverses three decisions you locked in `SCOPE.md`** - undo moves server-side (`:210-211`), the server starts pushing changes to browsers (`:223-224`), and the CLI gains write verbs (`:217`, `:225`, admitted in 2026-06-13 only on the condition that it "adds no mutation path") - *recommendation: amend all three in the milestones that break them, and answer the write-CLI question deliberately rather than as tooling convenience.*

3. **Global undo means an agent can reverse your work and you can reverse an agent's - and from M2 one browser tab can reverse another's, with no way to tell which.** *Recommendation: yes, but only with `expect` mandatory on undo, an `undo {to: seq}` bulk reversal, a reclaim hold the agent cannot race, and a per-writer `actor` field - otherwise the mitigation D2 promises cannot be built.*

4. **Three of the seven questions the plan asks you - log depth, the `catchup` optimisation, the content fingerprint - the plan already answers in its own words.** *Recommendation: take them back as substrate rulings and spend the attention on decisions 1-3 instead.*
